How to Build Your Own Galaxy 'Pause Point' Alternative Using One UI

Understanding the Pause Point Feature

Pause Point is designed to disrupt habitual phone scrolling by intercepting users right before a distracting feed loads. According to reports, the feature introduces an unskippable delay or prompts a brief pause—such as breathing exercises—when opening targeted apps. Deactivating it reportedly requires a full device restart, creating a significant hurdle during moments of temptation.

While the feature has reportedly expanded to various devices through updates like Android 17 QPR1 and specific vendor betas, many Samsung Galaxy users are still waiting for official availability.

Creating a DIY Stand-In with One UI Tools

While waiting for native support, Galaxy users can combine existing Samsung features to replicate aspects of the pause mechanism:

  • App Timers: Navigate to Settings > Digital Wellbeing and parental controls > App timers to set strict daily limits on distracting apps. Setting a limit to one minute can quickly block access, though Samsung's interface currently allows users to easily bypass the restriction with a tap.
  • Modes and Routines: Under Settings > Modes and Routines, users can set up custom Focus modes to restrict apps, though this requires manual activation or scheduling in advance.
  • Automated Routines: To react instantly when an app opens, go to the Routines tab:
  • Set the If condition to "App opened" and select your target apps.
  • Set the Then action to enable system-wide grayscale (found under Settings > Accessibility > Vision enhancements) to remove engaging colors.
  • Add an action to trigger Edge lighting for a jarring visual alert the moment the app launches.

Practical Implications and Verification

Homemade workarounds lack the strict safeguards of a native operating system feature, such as mandatory device restarts to disable restrictions. However, these custom routines offer a practical stopgap to interrupt mindless scrolling until official updates roll out to Galaxy devices.
